messages.subject: different facet_plot panel widths
parts:
Hi, Would it be possible to allocate different panel widths to facet-plot object?

Currently it is evenly calculated, as 1/2 each for two panels, 1/3 each for three panels, etc..

It'd be great if we can set it a relative widths, for example 2:4:3 for tree:geom_box:geom_violin.

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: e653eb797a0bfda9
messages.subject: Re: different facet_plot panel widths
parts:
Hello, 

I have looked for a solution to this but can't see any answers? I am sorry I have missed it already in the user group.

Below is an example tree

#install packages
library(ggtree)
library(reshape2)

# create tree
set.seed(123)
tree <- rtree(30)

# plot tree
p <- ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none") + 
  geom_tiplab()

# make structure-like data
a <- runif(30, 0,1)
b <- 1 - a
df <- data.frame(tree$tip.label, a, b)
df <- melt(df, id = "tree.tip.label")

# plot tree with structure data
facet_plot(p + xlim_tree(8), panel = 'bar', data = df, geom = geom_barh, 
           mapping = aes(x = value, fill = as.factor(variable)), width = 0.7, stat='identity')

It produces a plot like the attached photo. Is it possible to change the relative widths of each panel?

Many thanks for all the help

Best wishes
Ollie

messages.author: aa76bc9ea2907e22
messages.subject: Re: different facet_plot panel widths
parts:
Hi Gehoon and Ollie

I was able to do this with the grid and gtable package.

I got this from the following stack overflow thread:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49110877/how-to-adjust-facet-size-manually

I used Ollie's code as an example. see below

library(ggtree)
library(reshape2)

set.seed(123)
tree <- rtree(30)

# plot tree
p <- ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none") + 
  geom_tiplab()

# make structure-like data
a <- runif(30, 0,1)
b <- 1 - a
df <- data.frame(tree$tip.label, a, b)
df <- melt(df, id = "tree.tip.label")

# plot tree with structure data
p2 <- facet_plot(p + xlim_tree(8), panel = 'bar', data = df, geom = geom_barh,
mapping = aes(x = value, fill = as.factor(variable)), width = 0.7, stat='identity')

# load the packaged
library(grid)
library(gtable)

gt = ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p2))
gtable_show_layout(gt) # will show you the layout - very handy function
gt # see plot layout in table format
gt$layout$l[grep('panel-2', gt$layout$name)] # you want to find the column specific to panel-2
gt$widths[7] = 0.5*gt$widths[7] # in this case it was colmun 7 - reduce the width by a half
grid.draw(gt) # plot with grid draw


Hope it works for you!

Cheers

Pete
